title: Abstract Factory pattern
idea: The Abstract Factory pattern gives you one interface that creates a whole family of related objects, so everything a client uses is guaranteed to match.

analogy.text: A furniture shop sells matching collections. Choose the oak collection and the table, chairs and shelf all arrive in oak.
analogy.breaks: Shoppers can mix collections; an abstract factory makes mixing hard on purpose.

points: An abstract factory is an interface with one create method per product.
Each concrete factory returns one consistent family, like `UkKit` or `IndiaKit`.
Adding a family is one class; adding a product type edits every factory.
A JDBC `Connection` acts like one: its statements all match its driver.

code.title: The problem: mixed parts
code.caption: Three products wired one by one: a single wrong setting mixes two regions silently.

walk.text: The caller picks each product by hand. Rupee formatting slipped into a UK shop.
Three product interfaces. Each is fine; the danger is combining them.
An Indian formatter is a valid `MoneyFormat`, so the compiler accepts it.
The constructor takes three independent parts and cannot check that they belong together.
UK tax, UK postcode, Indian currency: the output is wrong, with no error.

code.title: The fix: one kit
code.caption: A `RegionKit` creates the whole family, so `Checkout` gets parts that match.

walk.text: The abstract factory: one method per product type in the family.
`UkKit` returns only UK products. Lambdas work because each product has one method.
`IndiaKit` is the second family. A third region is one new class plus one `case` in `kitFor`.
`Checkout` takes one kit and asks it for every product it needs.
Only `kitFor` names concrete kits. An unknown region fails fast with a clear message.
Each family validates its own way: a UK postcode fails the Indian rule.

pitfalls: Letting callers build products directly again brings back mixed families; route creation through the kit.
An abstract factory for one product type is ceremony; one factory method is enough.
Kits sharing one mutable product leak state between clients; return fresh or immutable objects.

quiz.q: Every region now also needs an `InvoiceTemplate`. What must change?
options: The RegionKit interface and every concrete kit
Nothing: kits can create any type
quiz.why: A new product type means a new method on `RegionKit`, which every concrete kit must implement. New families are cheap; new product types are not.

takeaway: One factory per family keeps every created part consistent.
